userStories.title: Phase 2 - Structured Block System
userStories.description: The backend sync outputs observations and interventions wrapped in custom block codes, and the frontend parses them into formatted card elements.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend sync generates custom ```observation-block and ```intervention-block formatted strings
Frontend HealthWikiRenderer parses these code blocks instead of rendering them as raw code
Observation and intervention blocks are rendered as custom cards with distinct styles
Negative cases: If block yaml is corrupted, fall back to simple note card rendering without crashing the application
userStories.notes: Custom markdown parsing wrapper (observation-block and intervention-block) added to HealthWikiRenderer.jsx. Generates interactive cards in UI with strong validation fallback.

userStories.title: Phase 3 - Attention Score System
userStories.description: Implement a quantitative server-side Attention Score calculation and connect it to dynamic visual glows in the frontend.
acceptanceCriteria: Observation blocks contain calculated attention_score (0.0 to 1.0) in YAML metadata
Backend assigns high scores to severe physiological markers or acute neurological deficits
Frontend maps attention scores dynamically (high scores trigger a red heartbeat shadow glow)
userStories.notes: Heuristics-based quantitative attention scoring added to backend sync. Frontend maps high-attention blocks (>= 0.8) to pulsating red shadow glow cards.

userStories.title: Phase 4 - Multi-stage AI Pipeline
userStories.description: Refactor the backend sync controller into sequential stages with transaction isolation and rollback on failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Sync API executes in sequential stages (Extraction -> Structuring & Scoring -> Assembler & Write)
API errors (e.g. rate limit/parse error) trigger transactional rollbacks, preventing partial writes to disk
userStories.notes: Sync logic split into Stage 1 (Extract), Stage 2 (Score), and Stage 3 (Assemble/Write) with error-rollback safety wrapping.
